title: STDP basics
summary: The synapse grows or shrinks depending on which spike came first.

terms.plain: who spiked first changes the synapse
terms.definition: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity. The sign of the synaptic change depends on the order of the presynaptic and postsynaptic spikes.
Long-term potentiation. Here, it is the increase when the presynaptic spike comes just before the postsynaptic spike.
Long-term depression. Here, it is the decrease when the postsynaptic spike comes first.

terms.plain: only the two spikes at this synapse
terms.definition: A rule that needs only information available at the synapse, not a broadcast of the whole network’s error.

cards.text:
Call the incoming spike “pre” and the receiving neuron’s spike “post”.
The synapse can see both.

Pre just before post: the link grows. That is LTP.
Post before pre: the link shrinks. That is LTD.

lines: Pre at 5 ms, post at 8 ms. Pre was first. The synapse grows.
Post at 5 ms, pre at 8 ms. Post was first. The synapse shrinks.

question.prompt: Pre at 5 ms, post at 8 ms. The synapse…
choices: does not change, because both spiked
question.why: Pre before post is the potentiating order.
question.simpler: Ask only which spike happened first.

question.prompt: STDP needs a teacher to tell the synapse the network’s error.
question.why: The two spike times at that synapse are enough. That is what makes it local.
question.simpler: A local rule does not receive the loss of the whole network.

recall.question: Which order produces LTP in ordinary STDP?
recall.answer: Presynaptic spike just before the postsynaptic spike.

deeper.note: Markram, Lübke, Frotscher, and Sakmann paired connected cortical cells and found the order of the two spikes set the sign of the change.

paper.title: Regulation of synaptic efficacy by coincidence of postsynaptic APs and EPSPs
